summary: SLP (Service Location Protocol, RFC 2608) on 427/tcp+udp is currently unmapped in recce's per-service layer. The port is included in the enum-phase UDP sweep (`_UDP_BASIC_PORTS` in recce/core/scanner.py) so nmap -sV will fingerprint it if run as root, and vulndb.py carries one ESXi/OpenSLP advisory (CVE-2021-21974 + CVE-2019-5544 + CVE-2020-3992), but there is no recce/services/slp.py, no PORT_NAMES entry in svcdetect.py, and no _NAME/_PORT mapping in serviceenum.py. Nothing in the codebase issues SrvTypeRqst / SrvRqst / AttrRqst, parses SLPv2 replies, discovers Directory Agents, or turns advertised service URLs into cross-service pivots. This is a green-field service module that lands high-value passive intel (service catalogue, host inventory, ESXi build strings) with a small stdlib probe, plus a well-known amplification / RCE story worth flagging.

capabilities.name: port_registration_427
capabilities.description: Register 427/tcp and 427/udp in svcdetect.PORT_NAMES and serviceenum._PORT so an nmap-blank port gets an 'slp' / 'Service Location Protocol' label without any traffic. Currently missing — 427 is not in either table.

capabilities.name: slp_version_fingerprint
capabilities.description: Parse the Version byte (1 = SLPv1, 2 = SLPv2) and function-id of any reply already grabbed by nmap-sV/banner, and record 'openslp' when the AttrRqst response carries the OpenSLP signature (SrvRply/AttrRply length quirks, or an explicit 'openslp' string in attributes). Enables version-gated CVE decisions later.

capabilities.name: srvtyperqst_enumeration
capabilities.description: Send SrvTypeRqst (function-id 9) with service-type='service:' and scope='DEFAULT' to unicast 427/udp; parse the SrvTypeRply list of advertised service types (service:vmware-infrastructure, service:printer, service:cifs, service:nfs, service:jetdirect, service:directory-agent, …). This is the single most useful passive-shape probe — one packet, full service catalogue.

capabilities.name: srvrqst_url_enumeration
capabilities.description: For each service type from the previous step (or a curated seed set), send SrvRqst (function-id 1) and parse SrvRply (function-id 2) to extract every advertised service:URL. Each URL carries host, port, path, and often the product tag — the raw material every cross-service pivot below needs.

capabilities.name: attrrqst_leak
capabilities.description: AttrRqst (function-id 6) against each URL returns per-service attribute lists. On ESXi this exposes fields such as (product='VMware ESXi'), (version='7.0.3 build-20328353'), (uuid=…), (managementserver=…), (cimom=…) — precise build strings ideal for CVE mapping. On CUPS/JetDirect it discloses printer names and PPDs. Unauthenticated on the standard OpenSLP config.

capabilities.name: directory_agent_discovery
capabilities.description: SrvRqst for service-type 'service:directory-agent' (or listen for unsolicited DAAdvert function-id 8 on multicast 239.255.255.253) identifies DAs — a single DA typically aggregates every SA on the segment, so hitting it with SrvRqst pulls the whole network's advertisements in one shot.

capabilities.name: multicast_srvrqst_segment_sweep
capabilities.description: Send SrvRqst to multicast 239.255.255.253:427 (IPv4 SLP-scope) with an empty PRList; every SLPv2 speaker on the segment replies over unicast UDP. Yields sibling hosts recce did not target, straight from L2. Gated behind an --slp-multicast flag because it needs local L2 and generates broadcast traffic.

capabilities.name: esxi_openslp_cve_flag
capabilities.description: When SrvRqst/AttrRqst returns service:VMwareInfrastructure (or the ESXi cimom URL) AND the extracted ESXi build predates the CVE-2021-21974 fix line, raise the existing vulndb.py 'VMware ESXi exposed — OpenSLP pre-auth RCE' advisory with a concrete build citation instead of a bare product-name match. Same treatment for CVE-2019-5544 (heap overflow) and CVE-2020-3992 (UAF).
capabilities.protocol_reference: CVE-2021-21974 (ESXi 6.5/6.7/7.0 OpenSLP heap overflow); CVE-2019-5544 (OpenSLP heap overflow, MSF module); CVE-2020-3992 (OpenSLP UAF)

capabilities.name: slpreflector_amplification
capabilities.description: Any SLP responder answering unauthenticated AttrRqst over UDP is a candidate SLPReflector amplifier (CVE-2023-29552, BAF up to ~2200×, CISA KEV 2023). Flag every 427/udp responder with a 'reflected DDoS amplifier' finding regardless of vendor; remediation is disable SLP on the public interface or drop source-spoofed 427/udp.
capabilities.protocol_reference: CVE-2023-29552 (SLPReflector); RFC 2608 §5 (no source validation on UDP replies)

capabilities.name: scope_and_language_disclosure
capabilities.description: SrvRply carries the scope list (e.g. 'PROD-VMOTION', 'BLDG12-PRINT') and language tag; scope names routinely disclose site / environment structure that helps a tester map internal segmentation, and are worth capturing into host notes.

capabilities.name: runbook_and_external_tools
capabilities.description: Emit runbook rows for external verification: nmap NSE 'slp-info', slptool (openslp-server) 'slptool findsrvtypes' / 'findsrvs' / 'findattrs', and a Metasploit 'auxiliary/scanner/misc/openslp' entry for CVE-2019-5544 (do NOT invoke automatically — flag only). Mirrors ipp.py runbook() shape.

capabilities.name: tcp_fallback_probe
capabilities.description: SLPv2 permits TCP for replies larger than the MTU (Overflow bit in message header). Send the same SrvRqst to 427/tcp — many ESXi hosts answer TCP even when UDP is filtered by intermediate networks, so a TCP probe recovers coverage that a UDP-only sweep loses.

capabilities.name: auth_block_detection
capabilities.description: SLPv2 authentication blocks (RFC 2608 §9) are almost universally unimplemented — record their presence/absence in the reply as evidence of hardening. Presence of Auth Blocks on an ESXi host is a strong signal of a locked-down deployment; absence on any 427-responder is the norm and reinforces the unauthenticated-disclosure finding.

existing_coverage.notes: No recce/services/slp.py exists. 427 is NOT in svcdetect.PORT_NAMES nor in serviceenum._PORT/_NAME, so a blank-service nmap result on 427 gets no label and no per-service script mapping. Nothing in the tree sends SrvTypeRqst/SrvRqst/AttrRqst or parses SLPv2 wire format. The ESXi advisory fires only if nmap-sV happens to set a product string containing 'vmware esxi' — SLP itself is not the trigger.

cross_service_wire_candidates: service:URL list from SrvRply → seed cross-service scanners: service:http/https → recce/services/http.py, service:printer/ipp → ipp.py, service:cifs → smb.py, service:nfs → nfs.py, service:ldap → ldap.py, service:jetdirect → JetDirect flag, service:VMwareInfrastructure / service:wbem → treat host as ESXi/vCenter
product + version pairs from AttrRqst (esp. ESXi 'product'/'version'/'build') → vulndb.py product match with precise version-gate (CVE-2021-21974 line)
New IPv4 hosts learned from multicast SrvRply / DAAdvert on 239.255.255.253 → append to host inventory as sibling discovery (feeds scanner + msrpc/smb/etc.)
Directory Agent identity (DAAdvert URL + scope list) → seed a follow-up unicast SLP query that aggregates every SA in scope in one shot
Scope names and site tags (e.g. 'PROD-VMOTION', 'BLDG12') → host notes + segmentation map used by report + attack-path narratives
Printer names / share names / filesystem export names from AttrRqst → enrich existing smb/nfs/ipp findings with human-recognisable resource labels
SLP responders on 427/udp with unauth AttrRqst → SLPReflector amplification list (CVE-2023-29552), consumable by an eventual DoS/exposure summary tab
CIMOM / managementserver URLs from ESXi AttrRply → vCenter host address (feeds vsphere / port-443 web probing on the management-plane host)

recommended_findings.title: ESXi OpenSLP RCE (CVE-2021-21974 / CVE-2019-5544 / CVE-2020-3992) — build-gated via SLP AttrRqst

SLP Directory Agent aggregates network-wide advertisements

implementation_notes: Ship as recce/services/slp.py modeled on ipp.py's shape: is_slp() gate, wire-format helpers (_slp_header, _slp_srvtyperqst, _slp_srvrqst, _slp_attrrqst) using stdlib struct + socket only (no third-party deps — recce is air-gapped, per project_airgap.md), probe()/targets()/findings()/runbook()/findings_to_vulns()/analyze() following svcprobe.iter_probe budget+state contract. Two integration wires needed at the same time: (1) add 427 → ('slp','Service Location Protocol') to svcdetect.PORT_NAMES and (2) add 427 → 'slp' plus name 'slp' → 'slp' to serviceenum._PORT / _NAME so recce services and the enrich_port path both light up. Multicast SrvRqst must be flag-gated (--slp-multicast) and skipped in default runs because it needs local L2 and generates broadcast traffic — matches how udp_basic_scan() gates on root. Version-gate the existing vulndb ESXi advisory on the build string parsed here to avoid a false positive when a patched ESXi still answers SLP. No new binaries to bundle; slptool / nmap slp-info live in runbook rows only.
